evidence: quiet_hours.rs window_for() gates the two windows ASYMMETRICALLY: the weekday branch (:61 `if schedule.quiet_hours_enabled`) requires the master flag, but the weekend branch (:51 `if is_weekend && schedule.weekend_quiet_hours_enabled`) checks ONLY weekend_quiet_hours_enabled and never the master quiet_hours_enabled.

Consequence: a user with quiet_hours_enabled=false (quiet hours turned OFF) but weekend_quiet_hours_enabled=true and a weekend window configured (weekend_quiet_hours_start/end Some) still gets quiet hours ACTIVE on Sat/Sun. evaluate() returns active=true and the pipeline holds their weekend push notifications even though the user disabled the feature.

Reachable in production: notification_pipeline.rs resolve_push_quiet_gate (:385-402) calls quiet_hours::evaluate (:391) and treats state.active as authoritative with NO pre-gate on quiet_hours_enabled; notification_digest.rs:307 likewise gates purely on evaluate().active. So window_for is the sole gate and the master flag is silently ignored on weekends.

The asymmetry is the tell that this is an oversight, not intent: if the two flags were meant to be fully independent, the weekday branch would not need the `if quiet_hours_enabled` gate either. Effect is a real UX bug — time-sensitive weekend pushes held/delayed for a user who turned quiet hours off (not lost; released at the bogus window end via the pipeline release horizon), so Medium not High.

Fix shape: gate the weekend branch on the master switch too, e.g. require `schedule.quiet_hours_enabled` before considering either window (or explicitly document+test the intended flag relationship). Pure function, already has a `disabled_is_never_active` unit test scaffold in the same mod tests block — add a weekend-with-master-off case. Confidence medium (static read; hinges on quiet_hours_enabled being the feature master toggle, which the UI-facing granular_notifications route surfaces as an independent boolean).
